summary: Customer requests SIEM ingest sample with per-field TTL metadata, rollback/erasure proof, and replayable resumption tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Financial (enterprise) is onboarding Redwood audit events into their Splunk SIEM. They require: per-field TTL (time-to-live) metadata written into the export manifest so that downstream SIEM retention can trigger deterministic deletion; a verifiable rollback/erasure proof (signed per-batch manifest) that shows which event identifiers were removed and why; and resumption tokens that let Nimbus resume ingestion from a deterministic checkpoint for forensic replay.

Impact:
- Security/compliance team cannot complete legalhold mapping because export manifests lack field-level TTL mapping and erasure attestations.
- Customer has a regulatory deadline (data-retention audit) in 10 business days.

Requested deliverables:
1) A sample NDJSON batch (1 hour window) showing: event envelope, per-field metadata TTL values (ISO8601 expiry), pseudonymization tag, and the per-batch HMAC and signed manifest.
2) Signed rollback/erasure manifest format example (showing event IDs, cause code, legalhold crosswalk id) and verification steps.
3) Resumption token format and instructions to resume from an offset (including how offsets are anchored to UTC and sequence numbers).
4) Example Splunk HEC ingestion snippet and a minimal validation script to verify chain integrity.

Notes on constraints from customer:
- They require manifests signed with a customer-acceptable attestation string and an HMAC anchored to the exported object ETag.
- They will not accept any export that exposes raw PII; any sensitive fields must be pseudonymized with the reversible-pseudonymization token ID included in the manifest for legalhold exceptions.
